PullRequest.Title: smoke: give new Integrated Browser pages time to commit their first navigation
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #344590

## Why

`Integrated Browser › navigates, reloads, and exposes page history` fails intermittently on the Windows large runners with `Timed out waiting for new page matching 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/navigation/a'`, and only the workbench is listed among the open pages.

The page isn't lost; it's slow. Playwright attaches to a new Electron `WebContentsView` straight away, but only reports it as a page (in `electron.windows()`) after its first navigation commits. Before that, a renderer has to start and the first request of a fresh browser session has to complete. `waitForNewPage` allowed 10s for the action plus that discovery.

In all three failing runs, the runner was stalled when the suite started. The two passing re-runs of the same commit show no stall:

| Signal | Failing runs | Passing re-runs |
|---|---|---|
| Copilot Chat activation | 22.7s / 18.7s / 19.1s | 5.2s / 5.2s |
| Agent host `sessions_v2 import` (0 sessions, 0 db opens) | 1.9–11.8s | 0.13–0.44s |
| Saving the failing test's trace (~600 KB) | 17.6s / 9.9s / 12.0s | — |

The last trace frames before the timeout show a `Browser` tab with a loading spinner and the typed URL, but no page content yet. The issue's screenshot of the loaded page was taken 10–18s after the timeout, because saving the trace took that long.

## What changed

- **Longer default wait:** `waitForPage` and `waitForNewPage` now wait 30s by default instead of 10s. That is Playwright's default timeout, which every locator and navigation wait that follows them in this suite already uses.
- **More useful timeout error:** it now includes the time waited and the browser's CDP page targets (URL and title). A target with the expected URL and an empty title means the navigation is still in flight. A real title means Playwright missed a page that had loaded. So a longer timeout can't hide a real attach problem.

## How to test

Run locally on macOS:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run compile --prefix test/smoke` | ✅ passed |
| `npm run smoketest-no-compile -- -g "Integrated Browser" --tracing` | ✅ 7 passing (run before rebasing onto `main`; the 8 new commits don't touch these paths) |
| `npm run eslint -- test/automation/src/playwrightDriver.ts` | ✅ passed |
| `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts test/automation/src/playwrightDriver.ts` | ✅ passed |

To reproduce the CI failure, I temporarily delayed the test server's first `/navigation/a` response; that change is not part of this PR. Command: `npm run smoketest-no-compile -- -g "Integrated Browser (opens an HTML|navigates, reloads)" --tracing`.
- **12s delay:** without this change, the test fails with the exact CI error and an identical screenshot. With it, ✅ 2 passing.
- **40s delay:** it fails after 30s with the new message, which lists the `/navigation/a` target with `"title":""`.

Not validated: the change hasn't run on Windows yet, and CPU stress on macOS didn't reproduce the stall. This PR's `Windows / Electron-Smoke (shard 2/3)` job is the real check.

Scenarios.Scenario: Smoke test opens an Integrated Browser or popup page and its first navigation commits successfully
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Playwright action opens the page, Electron starts the renderer and performs the local file/HTTP navigation, and the helper polls until the new Page is visible. The changed default deadline is only an upper bound; the helper returns on the same first successful poll as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The Integrated Browser performs its first navigation to the suite's local HTTP server (or loads a local file).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One navigation per discovered browser page; requests are serial within each test and the local server uses no-store responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same navigation was already required, but discovery failed after 10 seconds rather than allowing up to 30 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first navigation must commit before Electron exposes the WebContentsView as a Playwright page, so it controls discovery latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The test action and page discovery communicate with the Electron application through Playwright; getAllWindows checks the already tracked page list every 100 ms.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately one poll per 100 ms until the page commits; successful pages take the same number of polls as before, while pages committing between 10 and 30 seconds can now complete.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical polling and early return with a 10-second maximum.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery is on the test's critical path, but the changed deadline does not delay a successful match.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One awaited discovery per opened page; current callers perform one discovery in most tests and three serial discoveries in the lifecycle test. Polling remains every 100 ms, with effective work determined by navigation-commit latency rather than page count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each discovery is awaited serially within a test. No new parallel page creation, shared limiter, queue, or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Fresh browser sessions may pay cold renderer/network-stack initialization; warm or promptly committed pages return immediately. The change neither adds nor bypasses a cache and does not affect coalescing or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed lines only alter the deadline default, while the unchanged loop returns immediately on a match and all callers await it serially.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cold-start delay depends on runner load, but it does not change the mechanism: successful discoveries perform no additional polling beyond their actual commit time.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The longer bound converts slow 10-30 second commits from failed tests into successful tests without increasing normal successful-path latency or boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: A requested page never becomes discoverable
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The helper polls until its deadline, then gathers open URLs and now waits for one diagnostic CDP target query before throwing. Compared with the base revision, permanent failures can remain on the test critical path for 20 seconds longer plus up to 5 seconds for diagnostics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a CDP session, send Target.getTargets, and detach the session to describe page targets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one query after a helper reaches its final timeout, independent of the number of targets; results are filtered and serialized once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The helper threw immediately after collecting the locally tracked open URLs and made no CDP diagnostic request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduced on the error-reporting critical path and bounded by a 5-second race timeout; it is never reached on successful discovery.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most about 300 polling iterations instead of 100 for each failed helper invocation. Each failed test generally has one active invocation, and the lifecycle test cannot advance to later invocations after an earlier await fails.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Polling is serial. The timeout diagnostic races one CDP request against one 5-second timer; there is no per-target fan-out or concurrent batch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates. A permanent miss is not negative-cached because the test throws; the diagnostic runs once after the final miss.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the increased deadline and one-shot CDP boundary are explicit in the changed lines, and all repository callers are test-only, awaited invocations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A sustained product break could add 20-25 seconds to each affected failed smoke test, but this is a bounded, intentional failure-detection tradeoff and does not affect passing runs.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The additional wait is the stated reliability budget for a known realistically slow first commit, and the new failure-only diagnostic is a single bounded IPC operation rather than fan-out or unbounded work.

Scenarios.Scenario: The failure-only CDP diagnostic completes quickly or hangs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the page wait has already failed, describePageTargets races Target.getTargets against a 5-second timer, filters page targets, serializes URL/title pairs, and contributes them to the thrown error. This work is off every successful test path but on failure reporting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request all CDP target metadata over a temporary Playwright CDP session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser-wide request, not one request per target; filtering and JSON serialization occur in process once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No target enumeration or target metadata serialization occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can extend only the eventual timeout error by up to five seconds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Target.getTargets response containing the browser's target list; serialization grows linearly with open page targets, which are few and cleaned after each test.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One CDP operation and one timer are active. If CDP wins, the timer remains pending until five seconds but does no repeated work; if the timer wins, the unresolved CDP promise is not multiplied and its session cleanup remains owned by getCDPTargets when it settles.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caching or coalescing is relevant because diagnostics execute at most once per timed-out helper.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path, race bound, temporary-session detach, and single-response processing are directly visible in the code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact target-list size and CDP response time vary, but current smoke-test lifecycle bounds open pages and cleanup clears them after each test.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable boundary fan-out, retention, or cleanup-lifecycle regression. The diagnostic is bounded, failure-only, and uses one aggregate CDP request.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and all repository callers. The PR increases only the maximum failure/slow-navigation budget; successful page discovery returns at the same poll as before. The added target diagnostics issue one bounded aggregate CDP request only after timeout, with no realistic fan-out, concurrency burst, cache regression, or unbounded retention. No performance finding was submitted.
